extracted.intended_audience: readers of Popular Science Monthly — educated general public, natural philosophers, scientists, and students
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and normative statements for judging scientific inquiry, exposition, and pedagogy as discussed in Popular Science Monthly editorials and correspondence. Covers methodological standards (experiment vs. intuition), what counts as explanation, qualities of scientific writing, and curricular/teaching judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete scientific explanation (trace to ultimate forces)
rubrics_metrics.description: A natural phenomenon is not considered fully explained until you have traced it back to the ultimate forces which are concerned in its production and its maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because we can never become cognizant of forces as forces but only of their effects, scientific explanation must pass beyond mere sense-perception to abstract conceptions that refer to unseen causes. Explanations that stop at sensory description are therefore incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of instruments, experiment, and analysis (empirical method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Science begins by devising instruments of scrutiny, experiment, analysis, and dissection and, by their diligent application, reveals inner workings and causes that mere intuition cannot reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial contrasts this with the poetic/artistic method: relying on direct intuition and the 'beautiful show' is insufficient. Experimental procedures that test and challenge sensory impressions are essential; rejecting experimental 'torture' of phenomena is criticized as anti‑scientific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical examination of the senses' trustworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: The organs of sense give information about external effects produced on them, but convey those effects to consciousness in a different form; thus one must examine what claim senses have to be trusted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The natural philosopher asks whether things pronounced alike are really alike and whether things pronounced different are really different. Sensory impressions are not an irrefragable authority and must be tested by further inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of observed facts so they explain one another (Goethe's demand)
rubrics_metrics.description: Goethe demanded that, as a preliminary to investigation, observed facts should be so arranged that one explains the other and that insight into their connection may be attained relying on the senses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial describes this demand as 'most attractive' but 'essentially wrong in principle' because it avoids abstract conceptions and ultimate causes. Include as a historical/methodological stance to be recognized and critiqued rather than adopted wholesale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for abstract conceptualization beyond sense-data
rubrics_metrics.description: To penetrate to the causes of phenomena one must take the step into the region of abstract conceptions (atoms, forces, movements) which are not objects of sense but defined by abstractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a necessary move in physical science; poets may recoil from it, but subordinating sensory 'show' to abstract theory is justified as the way to govern and use nature's 'levers and pulleys.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity, strict scrutiny, and attractiveness in scientific writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholarly works should be characterized by strict scrutiny, clearness, and attractiveness of exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describing Friedrich Mohr's writings: these features made his contributions widely appreciated. Good scientific writing should combine rigorous analysis with clear, engaging presentation to reach both specialists and educated readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical utility, simplicity, and accuracy of methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical methods and manuals are judged by their practical value: simplicity, accuracy, and readiness of execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mohr's 'Manual of Volumetric Analysis' succeeded because it made volumetric analysis simple, accurate, and comparatively ready in execution; such practical improvements that facilitate industry adoption and broad translation are marks of a valuable scientific contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive and frank critical commentary on standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical commentaries on standards (e.g., pharmacopoeias) should be comprehensive, replete with original research, and characterized by frank critical analysis of both excellences and defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mohr's two-volume commentary on the Prussian Pharmacopoeia is praised as a model: its value lay in detailed, candid appraisal combined with original contributions — a benchmark for scholarly revisions of standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curricular criterion: teach scientifically-grounded evolution, reject unscientific extrapolations
rubrics_metrics.description: Evolution, cosmological and biological, so far as it is scientific, is to be taught as part of science; however atheistic, illegitimate, unscientific conclusions or dogmatic deliverances that allegedly flow from unwarranted expositions find no favor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to college instruction: adopt and encourage scientific investigations and teach evolution where it is supported by science, but avoid endorsing unscientific or dogmatic assertions presented as necessary philosophical or theological implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish perennial truth from obsolete cultural trappings (in religion/social ideas)
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating religious or cultural systems, discriminate between the living body (perennial truths) and its accidental, temporary wrappings (creedal habiliments) which must be changed as society progresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dr. Haven's remark is presented as a general evaluative principle: do not venerate obsolete forms or external 'drapery' as if they were the essential truth. This is a criterion for assessing progressivism in belief systems and institutions.
